food: Colonists eat when they get hungry. They eat food they carry first. With a restaurant (the cook's building) they go there to eat, and the cooks keep it stocked from the warehouse; variety and better dishes make colonists happier. Without one, a hungry colonist asks for food through the request system, and couriers bring it from the warehouse if there is any; otherwise someone has to bring it. A plain chest put somewhere is not part of this: colonists don't look in it. Food that should feed the colony goes into the warehouse.
storage: The warehouse keeps the colony's goods in its racks, and couriers (deliverymen) carry things between the warehouse and the buildings that ask for them. Only what is in the warehouse's racks, or in a building's own storage, counts as the colony's stock. A chest that isn't part of a building is invisible to the colony. A bigger warehouse level holds more and serves more couriers.
requests: When a colonist or a building needs something, it posts a request. If the colony has it or can make it, the request system assigns it: couriers bring it from the warehouse, or a crafter makes it first. If nobody in the colony can provide it, it waits for a player to bring it; those requests show in the building's window and in the colony's request list. A colonist waiting for something often stands idle until it comes.
building: Buildings start as a hut block placed with its blueprint; a builder from a builder's hut then builds them, level by level, from work orders. The builder asks for every material through the request system and stops when something is missing. A builder can only build up to the level of their own builder's hut, and most buildings can't be upgraded past the town hall's level. Several work orders wait in a queue; the next one starts when the builder is free.
housing: Colonists need a home with a bed: residences (houses) have more beds at higher levels. A colonist without a home sleeps wherever they can and is unhappier for it. New colonists only come to the colony while there is free room for them.
jobs: Each workplace hires colonists for its jobs, by itself or by the player in its window. How well someone does a job depends on their skills: each job leans on two of them, and skills grow with work. Someone without a job idles and grows less happy. A job can be changed in the workplace's window.
happiness: Happiness comes from many things: having a home, food and its variety, health, safety (guards nearby), having work, and company. Unhappy colonists work worse. The colony's overview shows what drags each one down.
sickness: Colonists can fall ill. A hospital with a doctor treats them; some illnesses need a particular cure item, which the doctor asks for. Without treatment, a sick colonist works badly and gets worse.
research: Research happens at the university, by its researchers. Each research costs items, takes time, and unlocks better buildings, tools or abilities; some need others done first and a university of a certain level.
defence: Guards live in guard towers and barracks: they patrol, guard spots and fight raiders and monsters. Raids come as the colony grows, usually at night. Guards fight better with armour and weapons, which they ask for through the request system.
growth: The colony grows when there are free beds and enough food: newcomers arrive, and couples with a home may have children, who grow up into colonists. The town hall's level limits how far other buildings can be upgraded.
